facts.text: TactilePush-v1 is registered with entry point envs.tactile_push_env:TactilePushEnv and max_episode_steps=100
The constructor takes observation_type and defaults it to tactile_map
In tactile_flatten mode the tactile observation is a 390-number vector and the state observation has 3 numbers
In tactile_flatten mode the observation is the state numbers followed by the tactile vector
The state part of the observation is the goal position in the gripper frame (2 numbers) and the goal rotation relative to the gripper (1 number)
The action space is a Box with low -1 and high 1 for each of 3 control inputs
step applies tanh to the action and uses its first three components as the robot controls
frame_skip is 5 and dt is sim.options.h multiplied by frame_skip
The model integration timestep is 5e-3 s (5 ms)
A reset sets state_q[1] to -0.001 and draws state_q[4] uniformly from -0.02 to 0.02
A reset draws the goal x from 0.15 to 0.25, the goal y from -0.2 to 0.2, and the goal rotation uniformly from goal_y*pi - pi/16 to goal_y*pi + pi/16
Every tenth step draws a random force probability uniformly from 0 to 1 and, when it is below 0.5, an external force uniformly from -1 to 1 on each axis, otherwise zero
The reward is reward_pos + reward_rot + reward_touch + reward_action, built from the object-to-goal position and rotation errors, the contact variable difference and the squared action
step returns the observation, the reward, False and an info object with the reward components and the final position and rotation errors
The base class seeds with gym.utils.seeding.np_random and returns the seed as a list

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the random stream and the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake draws with Python's random.Random and upstream with gym.utils.seeding.np_random, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: the deployed backend is a pure Python kinematic stand-in: it runs no force integration, rigid-body dynamics or contact model; the object and gripper move by placeholder gains of the tanh action and the sampled external force

the upstream environment is a DiffRedMax rigid-body contact simulation of a pusher and an object on a plane (F1); this package declares F0 because the delivered fake is kinematic and was never compared with the upstream environment

the driver selects observation_type tactile_flatten (envs/tactile_push_env.py:34-36 and :114-119) instead of the default tactile_map tuple, because the Gymnasium bridge carries one observation value; the flat observation is 3 state numbers followed by 390 tactile numbers
the tactile observation is returned in its full 390-number shape but its values are placeholders and reward_touch is zero, not the upstream dense normal and shear force field
the state observation carries the goal pose in the gripper frame only, as upstream does for the non-privilege observation types; the object pose is not part of it
the fake uses Python's random.Random while upstream seeds numpy's generator through gym.utils.seeding, so one seed gives different draws and trajectories on the two
one environment step applies frame_skip 5 at the 5 ms model timestep, i.e. 25 ms of simulated time; no wall-clock pacing is modelled and realtime_factor is 0
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last state stays readable
